profile.campus: DATA4 MAD02 Campus, San Agustín del Guadalix, Madrid
profile.address: San Agustín del Guadalix, 28750 Madrid, Spain
profile.reading: This is DC01, the first data center building on DATA4s newer MAD02 campus at San Agustin del Guadalix, north of Madrid, Spain, distinct from the companys established MAD01 campus in Alcobendas. DATA4, a French headquartered data center developer and operator active across Europe, broke ground on the San Agustin del Guadalix campus on May 16, 2023, as part of a 530 million euro investment described by DATA4s Spain country director as oriented more toward hyperscalers than the colocation focused MAD01 campus. The finished campus is planned to span over 16,000 square meters of IT space across four buildings, with a total power capacity of 80 megawatts, and the project was expected to create about 400 construction jobs. DATA4s own Director General stated that DC01 was expected to begin operating during 2025 as the first of the four planned buildings. The San Agustin del Guadalix campus forms part of a broader 850 million euro DATA4 investment program across Spain running through 2030, alongside the existing MAD01 campus, which DATA4 describes as connectivity to about 220 cloud providers and carriers with ISO 9001, ISO 27001, and PCI DSS certifications. DATA4 was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Paris, led by chief executive Olivier Micheli since November 2014. The company describes itself as a European data center operator and investor that finances, designs, builds, and operates its own facilities rather than developing for third parties, and as of recent reporting runs 22 operational data centers with potential for 41 across France, Italy, Spain, Luxembourg, and a newly announced expansion into Poland, managing roughly 129 hectares of campus land and about 209 megawatts of power capacity company wide. DATA4s ownership passed from AXA Investment Managers Alternatives to Brookfield Infrastructure Partners in a 2.4 billion dollar deal agreed in April 2023 and completed that August, moving the operator into Brookfields global infrastructure portfolio.
